comments.comment:
Nc6 transposes into 2... Nc6 3. Bf4
e6 4. e3 Bd6
5. Qf3 Nf6
Against the rarer moves, g4 as usual: (5... a6 6. g4) (5... c6 6. g4) (5... c5 6. g4 cxd4 7. exd4)

comments.at: 1. Nc3 d5 2. d4 Nf6 3. Bf4 e6 4. e3 Bd6 5. Qf3 Bxf4 6. Qxf4
comments.comment:
Against the rarer moves, g4 as usual: (6... a6 7. g4) (6... c6 7. g4 O-O 8. Nf3) (6... c5 7. g4)
Against ...Nbd7, Nb5 hits c7, which only the queen guards: (6... Nbd7 7. Nb5 O-O 8. Qxc7) (6... Nbd7 7. Nb5 e5 8. dxe5)

comments.at: 1. Nc3 d5 2. d4 Nf6 3. Bf4 e6 4. e3 Bd6 5. Qf3 Bxf4 6. Qxf4 O-O 7. g4
comments.comment:
g5 drives the f6-knight away: (7... Nc6 8. g5) (7... Nbd7 8. g5)
Against ...e5, take: after ...Nxg4, Be2 hits the knight. (7... e5 8. dxe5 Nxg4 9. Be2)

comments.at: 1. Nc3 d5 2. d4 Nf6 3. Bf4 e6 4. e3 Bd6 5. Qf3 Bxf4 6. Qxf4 Nc6 7. Nb5
comments.comment:
Sets up a trap, but it's not a bad move even if
black responds correctly. Remember to take with the queen: (7... O-O 8. Qxc7 Qxc7 9. Nxc7 Rb8 10. Nb5)
The other replies also cost Black the c7-pawn, except ...Kd7, which guards it: (7... a6 8. Nxc7+) (7... Nb4 8. Qxc7) (7... Nh5 8. Qxc7) (7... Bd7 8. Nxc7+) (7... Kd7 8. Nf3)

comments.comment: Other knight moves: (8... Nh5 9. Qf3 g6 10. Qxd5) (8... Nd7 9. e6)

comments.at: 1. Nc3 d5 2. d4 Nf6 3. Bf4 e6 4. e3 Bd6 5. Qf3 Bxf4 6. Qxf4 Qd6 7. Qxd6 cxd6 8. Nb5
comments.comment:
The knight eyes c7 and d6. After ...Kd7, a3, and the knight drops back once ...a6 comes: (8... Kd7 9. a3 a6 10. Nc3)
If c7 or d6 is left unguarded, the knight takes: (8... Na6 9. Nxd6+) (8... Ke7 9. Nc7)

comments.at: 1. Nc3 d5 2. d4 Nf6 3. Bf4 e6 4. e3 Bd6 5. Qf3 O-O 6. g4
comments.comment:
Bxf4 likely transposes
Otherwise g5 drives the f6-knight away: (6... Nc6 7. g5) (6... Nbd7 7. g5) (6... h6 7. g5)
Against ...b6, take on d6 first: (6... b6 7. Bxd6)
Against ...Bb4, Ne2 keeps our pawns intact: (6... Bb4 7. Ne2)
Against ...e5, take: (6... e5 7. dxe5)
